settings.title: Quality settings
settings.subtitle: Quality control decisions: when inspection is mandatory and who may judge quality

q1.title: 1. At what level is inspection done?
q1.help: Defines what is required before an order is released.
q1.final_only: Final inspection of the manufacturing order
q1.stages_and_final: An accepted in-process inspection for every stage with WIP, plus a final inspection

q2.title: 2. Is inspection mandatory before completion?
q2.help: When on, an order completes only from "Under inspection" after an accepted final inspection, and the completed quantity cannot exceed the released quantity.
q2.routing_flagged: Mandatory for orders whose routing has an inspection operation

q3.title: 3. Which decisions can an inspector make?
q3.help: Scrap and rework are always available for rejected quantity.
q3.allowConditionalHint: Also requires the manufacturing.quality_inspections.approve_conditional key ("Quality Manager" template).

q4.title: 4. Scrap accounting
q4.body: Not enabled in this release: dispositions are recorded as data only; abnormal scrap is not posted to the general ledger and rejected units do not move in inventory. Scrap accounts need review before this is enabled.

q5.title: 5. May people who produced an order inspect it?
q5.help: Whoever created the order, recorded its stage WIP, issued its materials or operated its work orders cannot inspect it.
q5.label: Enforce segregation of duties

q6.title: 6. Are organization admins subject to these controls?
q6.help: When on, everyone including admins needs an explicit role to inspect, and segregation of duties applies to them.
q6.label: Admins are subject to quality controls
